Senses.Explanation: A communal summons calls the whole assembly to a shared assigned activity. Monastic regulations use it for collective labor and explain that all ranks share the work. Chan hall addresses redeploy the same summons formula in “strike the drum and summon everyone to look”: look names the assigned action, while the headword still denotes the communal call. The institutional call remains the common referent across labor, attendance, and rhetorical redeployment.
Senses.Note: Ten anchors preserve regulations, work scenes, headings, narrative usage, and three distinctive hall-address redeployments of the communal summons.

Occurrences.Kwic: 普請之法蓋上下均力也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Document/heading metadata. Imperially Revised Baizhang Monastic Code (勅修百丈清規), redacted by Dehui: the regulations directly define the general work summons as upper and lower sharing the labor equally.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The monastic-code section heading and rule 普請之法蓋上下均力也 are procedural prose defining the summons; no encounter speaker utters them.

Occurrences.Kwic: 分付堂司行者報眾掛普請牌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Document/heading metadata. Imperially Revised Baizhang Monastic Code (勅修百丈清規), redacted by Dehui: the regulations tell the hall attendant to notify the assembly and hang the general-summons placard.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The rule 分付堂司行者報眾掛普請牌 is procedural prose directing the hall attendant to notify the assembly and hang the summons placard.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師囙普請開田回問運闍梨開田不易檗云眾僧作務
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Baizhang Huaihai section: compiler narration sets Baizhang's question to Huangbo after the communal field-opening summons; Huangbo answers that the assembly monks were working.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 師因普請開田回 is the compiler's scene-setting clause before Baizhang Huaihai questions Huangbo Xiyun about opening fields; neither master's direct turn contains 普請.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問維那。今日普請作甚麼。對曰。拽磨。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), spoken by Nanquan Puyuan in his explicit section: Nanquan asks the disciplinarian what the day's summons will do and is told that it will pull the mill.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師因普請次。巡寮去。見一僧不赴普請。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compiler narration. Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dongshan Wuben of Yunzhou (筠州洞山悟本禪師語錄), concerning Dongshan Liangjie: the record narrates his inspection of the quarters during a general summons and his finding an unnamed questioner who did not attend.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 師因普請次，巡寮去 is compiler narration placing Dongshan Liangjie on his inspection during the summons; Dongshan's direct question starts 爾何不去.

Occurrences.Kwic: 因普請钁地次。忽有一僧。聞飯鼓鳴舉起钁頭大笑便歸。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Baizhang Huaihai section: the compiler narrates an unnamed monk hoeing during the communal summons, laughing at the meal drum, and returning; Baizhang then questions him.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 因普請钁地次 sets the narrated hoeing scene; Baizhang Huaihai's direct appraisal begins 俊哉 after the unnamed monk laughs and returns on hearing the meal drum.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Guishan Lingyou section: the occasion heading labels tea-picking as the communal summons before Guishan and Yangshan's exchange.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 普請摘茶 is the compiler's occasion marker before Guishan Lingyou and Yangshan Huiji exchange words while picking tea; it is not their direct speech.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今朝正月半。有則舊公案。點起數盌燈。打鼓普請看。看即不無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), full-moon hall address. Dahui Zonggao is the exact speaker who lights several lamps, says to beat the drum and call everyone to look, and then asks what happens when the lamps go out.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今朝正月半，燈月光撩亂，目前無一物，打鼓普請看。復云：刺破眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi (楚石梵琦禪師語錄), Lantern Festival hall address. Chushi Fanqi is the exact speaker who says to beat the drum and call everyone to look, then adds, 'Pierce through the eye.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸佛出身處，石上好栽花；打鼓普請看，大地舞婆娑。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Juelang Daosheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師語錄), hall address. Juelang Daosheng is the exact speaker who says that flowers can be planted on stone, calls everyone to look, and says the great earth dances.
